q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is August 15, 2026. NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 ended April 26, 2026 (already concluded). The earnings release and forward guidance for Q3 FY2027 would typically come in late August 2026 or early September 2026. Time to resolution: approximately 2-3 weeks.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA has already provided official forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 on May 20, 2026: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**, which implies a range of $89.18 billion to $92.82 billion.

The question asks what will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release. Since Q2 FY2027 has already ended and the guidance was already issued, the answer is already known with certainty to be approximately $91.0 billion (the midpoint of their guidance range).

However, there's an important ambiguity: Does the question ask for:
1. The actual revenue that will be reported for Q2 FY2027 (already known: ~$91B based on guidance)
2. The forward guidance for Q3 FY2027 that will be issued when reporting Q2 results

Given the phrasing "forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release," this most naturally refers to the forward outlook issued at the time of Q2 reporting, which would be guidance for Q3 FY2027.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Macro weakness**: Economic slowdown reducing enterprise AI spending
- **China restrictions tightening**: Further export controls reducing addressable market
- **Competitive pressure**: AMD, Intel, or custom silicon gaining market share faster than expected
- **Supply chain issues**: Manufacturing constraints limiting revenue
- **Customer inventory corrections**: If customers have over-ordered and need to reduce inventory
- **Guidance conservatism**: NVIDIA might guide lower than trends suggest to ensure beats

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Strong demand trajectory**: Q1 FY2027 was $81.6B (+85% YoY), Q2 guidance is $91B (implied +12% sequential)—sustained momentum could accelerate
- **Better-than-expected adoption**: AI workloads ramping faster than anticipated
- **Geopolitical relief**: China restrictions being eased or workarounds being found
- **Market share gains**: Winning more enterprise accounts than expected
- **Guidance beat history**: NVIDIA has "surpassed Wall Street's EPS estimates in its last four quarters"
- **Customer prepayment/urgency**: Customers pulling forward orders due to capacity fears

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

**Reliable data from the research provided:**
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue: $81.6 billion
- Q2 FY2027 guidance (already issued): $91.0 billion ± 2% ($89.18B - $92.82B)
- Q2 analyst consensus: $91.8 billion (range $90.3B - $96.7B)
- NVIDIA has beaten EPS estimates in last 4 quarters

**Sequential growth rate**: Q1 to Q2 shows ~12% sequential growth ($81.6B to $91.0B guidance midpoint).

For forward guidance on Q3 FY2027 (to be issued in August/early September 2026), I should expect:
- Continuation of strong but moderating growth (cannot sustain 85% YoY forever)
- If similar sequential growth: ~$102B
- If growth moderates to 8-10% sequential: ~$98-$100B
- Conservative guidance suggesting $95-$98B range

Given:
- NVIDIA's history of beating estimates and guiding conservatively
- The strong momentum in Q1 and Q2
- Analyst consensus at $91.8B for Q2 actual (suggesting possible upside)
- Likely Q3 guidance in $98-$105B range

The specified range is 99.5B to 115.5B, suggesting the forecast is asking about a future quarter's guidance (likely Q3) or potentially conservative/upside scenarios.

**My assessment**: Most likely Q3 guidance will be in the $100-$106B range, with the central estimate around $103B, reflecting:
- Continued strong AI demand
- Modest sequential growth (8-10%)
- NVIDIA's tendency to guide slightly conservatively but not excessively so

NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion for Q1 FY2027, which ended April 26, 2026, an 85% increase year-over-year [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). For Q2 FY2027, NVIDIA's outlook, released on May 20, 2026, projects revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This guidance does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

Analysts' consensus for Q2 FY2027 revenue is $91.8 billion, with estimates ranging from $90.3 billion to $96.7 billion [tickerleague.com](https://tickerleague.com/companies/NVDA/estimates). NVIDIA has surpassed Wall Street's EPS estimates in its last four quarters [barchart.com](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3449043/what-to-expect-from-nvidia-s-q2-2027-earnings-report).
